transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Um… yeah, thanks. I guess I came in because I’ve just been feeling really low for a long time. Most mornings I wake up and it’s already there, like this heavy gray feeling on me before I even get to the clinic, and it kind of follows me through the day. I’m trying to manage it, but… I thought I should probably talk to someone about it, if that’s okay.
How long have you been feeling this way most days?

Um… most days, I’d say it’s been a little over two years now. About two years and two months, I think. It kind of started after the staffing changed at the clinic and my schedule started rotating all over the place. I mean, I’ve tried to just adjust to it, but… yeah, it’s been going on that long.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where you didn’t need much sleep or felt like you were on top of the world?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like, “on top of the world” or not needing sleep because I felt great. I mean, I can get irritable sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had periods where I was unusually energized or anything like that. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, or any significant changes in your appetite or weight over this time?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I mean, I still try to do things when I’m supposed to, so I don’t know if I’d call it a big loss of interest exactly. I guess some things don’t feel as enjoyable as they used to, but… maybe that’s just stress? Appetite and weight-wise, I haven’t really noticed a major change, at least nothing I’ve been tracking. Does that answer it okay?
Have you noticed feeling fatigued or lacking energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing much physically or mentally?

Yeah… I guess I have noticed that. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but even after a day off, or if I sleep in, my body still feels kind of worn out. And then at work, after rooming patients and trying to catch up on charts, it’s like I don’t have much left in me. I’ll think about doing laundry or going to shoot hoops or messing with my electronics stuff, but I just… don’t have the energy. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you’re not worth much during these low periods?

Um… I don’t know. I mean, I can be hard on myself sometimes, like if I mess something up or feel like I’m not keeping up, but I’m not sure it’s more than normal. I wouldn’t say I feel worthless, exactly. Maybe just… disappointed in myself sometimes? I don’t know if that counts.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or have trouble sitting still, like you're restless inside during these low periods?

I don’t think so… not in a way I’ve really noticed. Like, I’m not pacing around or feeling like I can’t sit still, and I don’t think people have said I’m moving slower or anything. Maybe I’m a little sluggish sometimes, but I just figured that was normal tiredness. Is that what you mean?

Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day, along with other symptoms like loss of interest, changes in appetite or sleep, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s kind of why I came in. For a long time now, I wake up already feeling low, like there’s this heavy gray feeling on me before I even get to the clinic. And it pretty much follows me through the whole day. Is that what you’re asking?
Have there ever been times, even brief ones, when something good happened and your mood actually lifted a little, like you felt genuinely better for a while?

A little, maybe… like if something good happens I can smile or feel okay for a bit. But honestly, it doesn’t last that long. Most days I still wake up with that same low, heavy feeling, and it kind of follows me through the day, even when I’m trying to act normal at the clinic. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Can you recall any specific times when your mood seemed to react more strongly to positive events around you, like you felt genuinely better or even cheerful for a while, even if it didn’t last very long?

I’m trying to think of a specific time… I mean, I can have moments where I seem okay, like if something nice happens at work or someone’s kind to me, I might feel a little lighter. But I don’t know if I’d call it really cheerful.

Mostly it’s more that I wake up already feeling low, like that heavy gray feeling is there before I even get to the clinic, and then it just kind of stays with me through the day. Maybe it lifts a little here and there, but not in a big way. Does that make sense?
Can you think of a time when something good happened and your mood stayed better for a few hours or even a day, not just a momentary lift?

I’m not sure I can think of it lasting a whole day, honestly. Maybe I get a small lift if something goes well, but it’s hard to say it really stays.

Most of the time… I came in because this has been going on a long time, where I wake up already feeling low, like this heavy gray feeling is there before I even get to the clinic. And then it pretty much follows me through the whole day. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but that’s been the pattern. Does that answer it okay?
Would you say that your low mood has been present for most of the day, nearly every day, for the majority of the past two years?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s been about two years and maybe two months now. It started around when the staffing changed at the clinic and my schedule started rotating all over the place. Since then, it’s been there most days, for most of the day. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
Looking back over the past two years, would you say there were times when you completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, or when those things didn’t bring you any pleasure at all?

I’m not sure I’d say I completely lost interest, exactly. Like, I still know the things I used to enjoy are supposed to be nice, and sometimes I’ll try to do them.

But… I guess they don’t always feel the same. It’s more muted, maybe. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic or like I never enjoy anything at all, because that wouldn’t be fair. It’s just harder for things to really land, if that makes sense. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Looking back, would you say there were times when you had absolutely no interest in things you used to enjoy, like they didn’t matter to you at all?

I don’t think I’d say absolutely no interest, no. At least… not like they didn’t matter to me at all.

It’s more that I don’t get as much out of them, or I have to kind of push myself to start. But if you’re asking whether I stopped caring completely, I don’t think that’s quite right. I hope that makes sense.
